memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out and all who belong to her, in accordance with your oath to her." So the young men who had done the spying went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers and sisters and all who belonged to her. They brought out her entire family and put them in a place outside the camp of Israel. — Josh 6:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of judgment, mercy walks out alive. The spies keep their promise, going into Rahab's house and bringing out her entire family — father, mother, brothers, sisters, everyone belonging to her. The scarlet cord had marked her home, and now every person inside it is rescued from destruction. Grace kept its word.

What a picture of salvation this is. Rahab was a Canaanite, a woman with a shameful past, living in a doomed city. By every measure she should have perished with Jericho. Yet because she trusted God and acted on that trust, she and her whole household were saved. Faith, not background or merit, made the difference. If God's grace could reach Rahab, it can reach anyone.

Notice too that her faith brought her family to safety. Because Rahab believed and gathered her loved ones under the sign of the cord, they were spared with her. Our faith, while personal, is rarely private in its effects. When we trust God, we often become the means by which others are drawn toward His salvation too.

The New Testament honours Rahab twice — among the heroes of faith (Heb 11:31) and as one whose faith proved itself in action (Jas 2:25). And most wonderfully, she is woven into the family line of Jesus (Matt 1:5). The Saviour of the world came through a rescued Canaanite. That is the reach of God's grace, and it is offered still to all who trust Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does Rahab's rescue assure you that God's grace can reach anyone, including you?
2. How might your faith become a means of drawing your loved ones toward God?
3. What does it stir in you that Jesus' own family line includes a rescued outsider?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your grace reaches the most unlikely people. Like Rahab, help me trust You fully, and use my faith to draw my loved ones toward Your salvation. Amen.
